chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: Branca's and Frank's Steak House with Ronnie Cole
summary: Dance heard him with Ronnie Coles; they played long improvisations, at Branca's from June 1957 to '61, then Frank's, until tax trouble ended it.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: [PAUSE]
When I first heard you, you were playing at Frank's Steak House on Long Island with Ronnie Coles on drums, and Ronnie had a set of bells which he used very effectively.
Oh yeah.

Now, that was the first time that I heard anybody sort of playing and improvising on the organ at great length. I don't doubt, you know, some of the others did it. But I never heard... In fact, when we made records, you had one there about twenty minutes or more long.
[LAUGHS]
And it was very interesting.

In those days, Ronnie and I used to do 62 choruses of 'How High The Moon.' But we had nothing else to do, especially when the place had no people in there, you know. Of course, I opened up in Bolin's(?), or Branca's (we
Ramirez - 131
called it Branca's) in June 1957. I left the Baby Grand in Brooklyn at that time. And we stayed there until '61. From there on we went to Frank's Steak House.
How long were you at Frank's?
I don't think we... We were there for about a year or two. Not that long. At Branca's we stayed about three years.
There was quite a lot of recording done there. A friend of yours did it, didn't he. And he got very good results.
Yeah. That was the late... Boy, I'm telling you...
The thing is that the record of that that was taken from his recording, put out in Europe, it did cause quite a bit of noise over there, didn't it.
It certainly did.
I don't think it sold a lot. But, you know, critical types found it very, very good.

Yeah, I was surprised myself when I went over there and found out about it. John (?) sold quite a few. I don't know, Ronnie and I could never get...we never got together over there, both of us, you know, the way we used to play. It never came off that way. So he went over there with somebody else, I went over with someone... And the
Ramirez - 132
things that we did together, it was...we never really...
Well, you were a good team.
We were. And we were very popular here in New York State, up in New York State, and out to the Coast, the West Coast... We had a lot of invitations to go out there, you know. We were very successful.
Why did you break up? What was the end of that association?
I don't know. The place changed owners...
Oh, the business fell off there.
Yeah, business fell off. And there were other things involved, you know; some taxes and stuff. Internal Revenue trouble with the place all the way around, and he had to take a powder.
